subject: Post-demo: Decision criteria, signoff owners, and redline staging
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@cardinalhealth.com>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Decision criteria, signoff owners, and redline staging

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Decision criteria (what you told us)
- Latency: sub-150ms p95 for interactive clinician workflows
- Data controls: VPC + customer-managed KMS for PHI-adjacent records
- Unit economics: target token cost threshold for pilot at $0.0015/token

2) Who signs what (as I understand it)
- Economic buyer: Olivia Barnes / Sr. Dir, Clinical Ops (final purchase approval)
- Security/InfoSec: John Lee / Legal (security checklist + DPA signoff)
- Procurement: procurement@cardinalhealth.com (PO & payment terms)

3) Proposed legal routing (minimal friction path)
- NDA (if still needed) first, 48-72 hour turn target
- DPA review in parallel with NDA redlines, security attestation appendix
- MSA redlines last, with a 5-business-day internal review cadence from our side

4) Immediate asks / next actions
- Olivia: confirm who will own the PO cadence and target pilot budget range by EOD Friday
- John/Legal: can you share preferred MSA template or a link to redline locations so we can align our suggested edits?
- Procurement: please confirm invoicing contact and whether Cardinal requires a vendor packet prior to PO issuance

Attachments: small brief we promised (cardinal_requirements_brief.pdf) and a short redline template we typically use for pilot MSAs (redline_template_v1.docx).

If helpful, Ben can map a 3-week contracting timeline with handoffs and expected turn times. Happy to schedule a 30-min contracting sync this week.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@cardinalhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Decision criteria, signoff owners, and redline staging

Thanks Alex — great summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: we have a provisional pilot bucket of $45k; I'll confirm whether that converts to a PO or a one-off test purchase.
- Procurement contact: Sara Mullins (sara.mullins@cardinalhealth.com) is the PO owner; adding procurement alias for visibility.
- Legal template: we use a standard Cardinal MSA; John, can we share the MSA doc and list of non-starters on redlines?

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a conservative latency profile (p95) for 4k token context and a quantized med-L4 model variant? That will help my execs sign off on the economics piece. 

Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Sr. Dir, Clinical Operations | Cardinal Health
olivia@cardinalhealth.com | +1 (614) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@cardinalhealth.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, John Lee <j.lee@cardinalhealth.com>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Decision criteria, signoff owners, and redline staging

Appreciate the questions — pulled together a practical routing playbook below (keeps PR/Legal busy-work to a minimum while protecting controls):

Routing playbook (recommended):
- Step 0 (optional): Mutual NDA if any internal collateral will be shared (48-72 hour target)
- Step 1: Security evidence package (SOC2 Type II snapshot, encryption/KMS notes, data flow diagram) — we can send an initial packet within 24 hours of request
- Step 2: DPA review — we accept some of Cardinal's standard clauses; propose counter: data retention capped for pilot, strict access logs, and audit rights. Turn: 3-5 business days for initial redline pass
- Step 3: Procurement / PO: parallel to DPA but dependent on budget confirmation from Olivia; procurement to confirm vendor onboarding docs (W9, vendor form)
- Step 4: MSA redlines: our suggested sequence is to do high-level commercial terms first (SOW, pricing, term) then legal boilerplate. We propose a single consolidated redline file to avoid back-and-forth; internal review cadence: 5 business days from receipt

Turn-times we should commit to (proposed SLAs for pilot):
- NDA: 2-3 days
- DPA initial pass: 3-5 days
- MSA consolidated redline: 5 business days internal review, then exchange with Cardinal

Action items (owners):
- Alex: schedule contracting sync (30 min) this week — propose Fri 11:00 PT
- Olivia: confirm pilot PO path (PO vs credit card) and budget owner by Fri EOD
- Procurement: send Sara Mullins contact info and vendor packet checklist
- John: if you can share Cardinal MSA link, we'll pre-seed redlines on commercial/term items to speed the process

Attachments referenced: redline_template_v1.docx (template we typically seed).

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: John Lee <j.lee@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia@cardinalhealth.com>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Decision criteria, signoff owners, and redline staging

Thanks all — looping in a few internal notes from legal/security: 

- We'll upload the Cardinal MSA and standard attachments to a secure SharePoint link by EOD. Please use that doc as the source of truth for redlines.
- Non-starters: persistent broad data resale clauses, unlimited indemnity wording, and vendor-hosted key escrow. Anything we see along those lines will be flagged early.
- Turn times: Legal can commit to a 5-business-day initial redline turnaround for pilot agreements if we have a single consolidated redline file from Redwood. DPA reviews can be faster (3 business days) if you provide a security snapshot up-front.

One operational request: please include a short SOW paragraph in the MSA redline that limits scope to the pilot clinical-review workflows and explicitly excludes PHI storage; that will make security sign-off faster.

John Lee
Senior Counsel, Legal Operations | Cardinal Health
j.lee@cardinalhealth.com
